environment.atoll_server_storage: copied stopped server home including Channel ledger state
environment.artifact_storage: copied stopped daemon home containing the File Resource

verified_facts: a normal registered user can log in from the restored Atoll identity and ledger home
the restored Recruiting actor reads the clean restored MySQL database
the original Company command returns the byte-stable stored outcome instead of creating a second Company
the Company, historical Work, Artifact metadata, migration ledger, and delivered event intent survive
the restored runtime identity can serve the product but still cannot create a table
the domain event remains exactly once in the restored Atoll Channel ledger
the daemon-hosted Artifact returns the original 1728 bytes with the exact SHA-256 digest
database credentials are absent from the logical dump

scope.proved: a stopped, bounded three-plane fixture can be restored into clean MySQL and filesystem targets without breaking identity, command idempotency, ledger uniqueness, or Artifact referential integrity
scope.not_proved: production-volume RTO/RPO, online distributed snapshot coordination, encrypted off-site retention, binlog point-in-time recovery, remote Artifact providers, or region loss

acceptance_effect.reason: the three-plane mechanism gap is closed for a cold bounded fixture, while production scale, PITR, external executor throughput, and long-window SLO evidence remain
